column1: # SeaBSD linuxolator compatibility matrix (v0.1 draft)
# Fields (pipe-separated):
#   name      short identifier used in reports and logs
#   category  base | browsers | gaming | media | development | futex
#   optional  yes | no  - optional entries become SKIP when the binary is absent;
#                         required entries become MISSING
#   binary    absolute path (inside /compat/linux for Linux userland probes) or
#             a command name resolved via PATH (for FreeBSD-side launchers).
#             "@PROBES@/NAME" expands to $SEABSD_PROBES_DIR/NAME (default
#             /usr/local/lib/seabsd/probes) - static probe binaries built by
#             the CI linux-probes job from tools/probes/*.c
#   args      arguments passed to the binary (must not contain "|")
#   expect    POSIX extended regex matched against combined probe output;
#             this is the only field allowed to contain "|"
# Probe self-reporting: a probe binary may detect that a feature is not
# implemented on the host kernel and exit with code 77; the runner records
# SKIP (feature detection) instead of FAIL. See tools/probes/futex_stress.c.
# Rules for adding entries:
# - Probes must be non-interactive and safe to run on a user workstation.
# - Linux shell scripts CANNOT be executed directly by shebang: the linuxolator
#   does not translate script interpreters. Invoke scripts explicitly through
#   the base bash, e.g. binary=/compat/linux/usr/bin/bash, args="<script> ...".
#   (Found by the first CI matrix run: ldd is a script and returned exit 127.)
# - "base" entries always exist once a Linux base is installed: they verify the
#   linuxolator itself, before any application-level conclusions are drawn.
# - GUI launch tests are out of scope for v0.1 (see ROADMAP, "Lighthouse").
# - Paths may need adjusting to the Linux base in use; keep at least one
#   working "base" entry valid for the default SeaBSD Linux base.
# TODO(seabsd-v0.1): after the Linux base decision lands, verify every path
# below against the actual base layout and record results in docs/linuxolator.md.
# --- Linuxolator baseline (always run first) -------------------------------
base-coreutils|base|no|/compat/linux/usr/bin/ls|--version|GNU
base-bash|base|no|/compat/linux/usr/bin/bash|--version|bash
base-ldd|base|no|/compat/linux/usr/bin/bash|/compat/linux/usr/bin/ldd --version|ldd
linux-chromium|browsers|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/chromium|--version|Chromium
linux-firefox|browsers|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/firefox|--version|Firefox
# Steam is launched through the FreeBSD-side linux-steam-utils launcher; any
# non-empty output proves the linuxolator stack loads the launcher. Real game
# tests belong to the v0.2 sandbox track.
linux-steam|gaming|yes|/usr/local/bin/steam|--version|.
linux-ffmpeg|media|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/ffmpeg|-version|ffmpeg
linux-gcc|development|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/gcc|--version|gcc
linux-python3|development|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/python3|--version|Python
linux-git|development|yes|/compat/linux/usr/bin/git|--version|git version
# --- Futex (kernel futex paths, static probes from tools/probes) ------------
# futex-core: the wait/wake surfaces every threaded Linux program leans on
# (private flag, both timeout timebases, bitsets, requeue, contention).
# futex-waitv: futex_waitv (newer interface, may legitimately be ENOSYS on
# older hosts - recorded as SKIP). Plan and risk zones: docs/futex.md.
# Required entries: CI installs the probe binary and points SEABSD_PROBES_DIR
# at it; on a workstation without probes they are reported as MISSING.
futex-core|futex|no|@PROBES@/futex_stress|waitwake timed_rel timed_abs_mono timed_abs_rt bitset requeue contention|fail=0
futex-waitv|futex|no|@PROBES@/futex_stress|waitv|fail=0
